title: Automate AZ-aware subnet tagging and bootstrap split-horizon stub-zone for private control plane
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds AZ-aware subnet tagging, idempotent stub-zone bootstrap for split-horizon DNS, and optional ephemeral endpoint failover. Backwards compatible with existing control plane allocations.
description: Motivation: Private control plane deployments in multi-AZ customer VPCs occasionally surface drift where subnets lack the expected 'redwood:controlplane' AZ tags or the stub private hosted zone (split-horizon) is not provisioned to route control-plane traffic to the local AZ endpoint. This causes cross-AZ hairpinning and latency spikes when the control plane routes to a different AZ. This PR automates detection and safe remediation for those gaps during installer runs and enables a guarded bootstrap path for creating per-AZ stub zones and minimal route table associations when requested. What this changes: 1) terraform/installer: subnet-allocator module now writes/reads the new tag set redwood:cp-role, redwood:cp-az and a tagredwood:cp-enforced timestamp; an idempotent reconciler ensures missing tags are added without reassigning IPs. 2) dns/bootstrap: introduces a templated bootstrap worker (stubzone_bootstrap.sh) that creates private hosted zones with split-horizon delegations and associates them to target VPCs per-AZ if feature flag is enabled. 3) helm/patch: private-controlplane chart gains values.controlPlane.bootstrapStubZone=false by default and a jobs.cron job for emergency rehydration. 4) scripts/rollback: adds restore-subnet-tags.sh that safely reverses only tags the installer added within last 24h to support rollback. 5) tests: integration tests that simulate a two-AZ VPC with missing tags and validate no IP reassignments and correct route propagation. Backwards compatibility: New behavior is off by default and uses conservative IAM principals that only allow hosted-zone and tagging operations when explicitly enabled. Rollout plan: merge to main, ship as feature-flagged installer release; stage in canary customers with 1% enabling bootstrapStubZone; monitor routing latencies and the 'cp_tag_enforcement' metric exposed in console. Rollback plan: set bootstrapStubZone=false and run restore-subnet-tags.sh if a rehydration caused unforeseen issues. Checklist: [x] terraform module unit tests updated [x] integration tests added [x] docs updated with operator guide [x] feature gated in helm values [x] IAM policies scoped and documented Testing performed: local dry-run against a sandbox AWS account, integration tests in CI (mocked Route53), and a small canary deploy to staging where tags were rehydrated without IP churn. Related: ENG-2439 (subnet reconciliation), ENG-2491 (dns stub-zone design).
commits: add: subnet-allocator: expose cp tags and enforcement timestamp; add: dns stubzone bootstrap worker; fix: helm values default and job template; add: restore-subnet-tags rollback script; test: add integration test for az tagging; docs: private-deploy subnet tagging guide
